Loading Libraries

library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)

Loading Data

# Data from reddit user austingwalters in this reddit thread: https://www.reddit.com/r/udub/comments/4e6kxl/i_made_a_website_that_shows_grade_distributions/
# Dataset and FOIA info from their dropbox: https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fo/8lbyazjlt5jmv86jvvs06/AGtgMaWeyZtZuS2fSYLYn_4?dl=0&e=1&rlkey=1sg7t372nhslxogwjl3e9lt9t

uw_grades_original_df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kylethayer/Info-201-au-24-datasets/refs/heads/main/UW-Seattle_20110-20161-Course-Grade-Data_2016-04-06.csv", check.names=FALSE)
 
# From Course_Number get program abbreviation (Program_Abv) and number (Course_Number_Num)
# From Term get Term_Season
uw_grades_df <- uw_grades_original_df |> 
  mutate(
    Program_Abv = str_split_i(Course_Number, " ", 1),
    Course_Number_Num = as.integer(str_extract(Course_Number, "\\d+")),
    Term_Season = str_extract(Term, "Autumn|Spring|Summer|Winter")
  )

Overall Grade Distribution Summary

Courses in the dataset

num_courses <- 
  uw_grades_df |>
  nrow()

Average GPA across courses

average_gpa <-
  uw_grades_df |>
  pull(Average_GPA) |>
  mean(na.rm = TRUE)

Average number of students across courses

average_students <-
  uw_grades_df |>
  pull(Student_Count) |>
  mean(na.rm = TRUE)

Minimum number for a course

min_course_num <-
  uw_grades_df |>
  summarize(num = min(Course_Number_Num))
minimum <-
  min_course_num |>
  pull(num)

Maximum number for a course

max_course_num <-
  uw_grades_df |>
  summarize(num = max(Course_Number_Num))
maximum <-
  max_course_num |>
  pull(num)

Histogram of Average GPA

ggplot(uw_grades_df, aes(x = Average_GPA)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.1) + labs(title = "Average GPA for all courses", x = "Average GPA")

Scatterplot of Average GPA vs Student Count

ggplot(data = uw_grades_df) + geom_point(mapping = aes(x = Student_Count, y = Average_GPA)) + labs(title = "Average GPA vs Student Count", x = "Student Count", y = "Average GPA")

There are 39242 courses in the data set. The average GPA across all courses in the data set is 3.41. The average number of students across courses is 45.38. The minimum and maximum course numbers 100 and 750 respectively.

The Average GPA histogram appears to be skewed to the left with a midpoint between 3.0 and 3.5, which matches the average calculated above. The range of values is between 2.0 and 4.0.

In the Average GPA vs Student Count scatterplot, there are few classes with an average GPA less than 2.5 and more than a hundred students. Classes with an average GPA between 2.5 and 3.0 are more scattered for student counts of more than around 350 than smaller student counts, while classes with an average GPA greater than 3.0 are more scattered for student counts of more than around 250.

Histogram of average GPA for 2010

ggplot(uw_grades_df |> filter(Academic_Year == "2010-11"), aes(x = Average_GPA)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.1) + labs(title = "Average GPA for all courses in 2010", x = "Average GPA")

Histogram of average GPA for 2015

ggplot(uw_grades_df |> filter(Academic_Year == "2015-16"), aes(x = Average_GPA)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.1) + labs(title = "Average GPA for all courses in 2015", x = "Average GPA")

Scatterplot of Average GPA vs Student Count in 2010

ggplot(data = uw_grades_df |> filter(Academic_Year == "2010-11")) + geom_point(mapping = aes(x = Student_Count, y = Average_GPA)) + labs(title = "Average GPA vs Student Count for 2010", x = "Student Count", y = "Average GPA")

Scatterplot of Average GPA vs Student Count in 2010

ggplot(data = uw_grades_df |> filter(Academic_Year == "2015-16")) + geom_point(mapping = aes(x = Student_Count, y = Average_GPA)) + labs(title = "Average GPA vs Student Count for 2015", x = "Student Count", y = "Average GPA")

There were 6961 courses in 2010 and 4462 courses in 2015. The average GPA across all courses was 3.4in 2010 and 3.46 in 2015. The average student count across all courses was 44.1 in 2010 and 47.65 in 2015. In 2010 the amount of unique primary instructors was 2987. In 2015 it was 2412.

The 2010 and 2015 average GPA histograms are both similar to the overall average GPA histogram and similar to each other.

The 2010 and 2015 scatterplots are also both similar to each other and the overall scatterplot.

English average GPA

ggplot(uw_grades_df |> filter(Program_Abv == "ENGL"), aes(x = Average_GPA)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.1) + labs(title = "English Program Average GPA", x = "Average GPA")

Art course number vs student count

ggplot(data = uw_grades_df |> filter(Program_Abv == "ART")) + geom_point(mapping = aes(x = Student_Count, y = Course_Number_Num)) + labs(title = "Art Program Course Number vs Student Count", x = "Student Count", y = "Course Number")

English course number vs student count

ggplot(data = uw_grades_df |> filter(Program_Abv == "ENGL")) + geom_point(mapping = aes(x = Student_Count, y = Course_Number_Num)) + labs(title = "English Program Course Number vs Student Count", x = "Student Count", y = "Course Number")

The average GPA in the art program and the english program are 3.48 and 3.48 respectively. The average number of students in art program classes is 28.59. The average number of students in english program classes is 23.45. The art program has a minimum course number of 120 and a maximum course number of 581. The english program has a minimum course number of 102 and a maximum course number of 599. There are 969 in the art program and 2985 in the english program, about 2000 more than the art program.

The art program average GPA histogram is skewed to the left with a midpoint around 3.5 while the english program average GPA histogram appears to be less skewed but with a midpoint also around 3.5.

In the art program course number vs student count scatterplot most of the courses have a student count less than on hundred, but courses with a course number of 200 are various in student count. There are also some courses with course numbers less than 200 that have student counts between one and two hundred. The most students a course has is between three and four hundred.

In the english program course number vs student count scatterplot, most courses have a studnet count of less than 40. Courses with a course number around 300 and around 200 are more various in student count, the former having at most around 150 student and the latter having at most around 120 students. Courses with a course number of less than 200 have at most 80 students.

English classes and art classes have similar numbers of students, but there are no english classes with more than 200 students while there are a few art classes with more than 200 students.
